gallery.title: File:Merseyside Maritime Museum, Albert Dock, Liverpool - geograph.org.uk - 633029.jpg
gallery.description: Merseyside Maritime Museum, Albert Dock, Liverpool One of Europe's largest maritime museums housed in a Grade I-listed former warehouse designed and built by Jesse Hartley in 1846. Includes historic vessels and two historic quaysides. The displays reflect the history of the merchant navy, shipping from the 13th century and the development of the Port of Liverpool and its international links. The International Slavery Museum, opened in August 2007 on the third floor, tells the story of the transatlantic slave trade up to its abolition in 1807.

gallery.title: File:Project 366 -217 040824 Approaching Lift Off (53902389448).jpg
gallery.description:
With Laura working a night last night she spend the morning sleeping and so I took our Finnish guests out for a slightly unusual work.
We drove in the car to Sandhills Lane, walked along the canal to the Stanley Flight of staircase locks, then back up on to the dock road and past Bramley Moore to take in the new stadium.
It's looking a lot more complete and certainly very shiny. Both my visitors felt immediately that it looked like a Zeppelin. I can see why!

I hope it feels like 'ours' quickly.
